facts.statement: Serikornis fossils were found in the Upper Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: from the Upper Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China

facts.statement: Serikornis lived during the Late Jurassic, specifically the Oxfordian stage, between 163 and 156 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, entre 163 a 156 millones de años, durante el Oxfordiense

facts.statement: The name Serikornis means "Ge Sun's silk bird", referring to the plumulaceous-like body covering seen in the fossil.
facts.quote: Its name means "Ge Sun's silk bird", a reference to the plumulaceous-like body covering evident in the fossil

facts.statement: The specimen is nicknamed "Silky" because its delicate hindlimb filaments resemble the modern Silky breed of domestic chicken.
facts.quote: The specimen's nickname, "Silky", refers to the striking resemblance of the delicate hindlimb filaments to the modern Silky breed of domestic chicken

facts.statement: Serikornis is distinguished by having very large anterior maxillary teeth that are about twice as long as the others.
facts.quote: very large anterior most maxillary teeth, about twice as long as the others

facts.statement: The coracoid of Serikornis lacks the diagnostic ornamentation of Anchiornis but is elongated to form a crest.
facts.quote: the coracoid of Serikornis is devoid of diagnostic ornamentation present in Anchiornis but is distinguished by having the tuberculous coracoid elongated to form a crest

facts.statement: The skeletal morphology suggests Serikornis had a terrestrial ecology without flying adaptations.
facts.quote: The skeletal morphology of Serikornis suggests a terrestrial ecology without flying adaptations

facts.statement: The elongated hindlimb feathers suggest they evolved in ground-dwelling maniraptorans before being co-opted for an arboreal lifestyle or gliding.
facts.quote: elongated feathers of the hind limbs extend to the toes, suggesting that the remiges of the hind legs had evolved in the maniraptorans residing on the ground before being co-opted to an arboreal lifestyle and possibly, gliding

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Serikornis as a basal Paravian outside Eumaniraptora.
facts.quote: places Serikornis, along with other late Jurassic paravians from China, as basal Paraves, outside Eumaniraptora

facts.statement: Some studies place Serikornis in the family Anchiornithidae, grouping it with Eosinopteryx.
facts.quote: placed Serikornis in the newly described family Anchiornithidae, still being grouped with Eosinopteryx

facts.statement: Serikornis was first described in August 2017.
Some researchers believe Serikornis is a junior synonym of Anchiornis.
facts.quote: Some researchers believe it is a junior synonym of Anchiornis

facts.statement: In 2019, researchers questioned the validity of Serikornis's distinguishing traits, suggesting they might be misinterpreted or intraspecific variation relative to Anchiornis.
facts.quote: In 2019, the supposed distinguishing traits of Serikornis were called into question. Their validity was questioned because they were either misinterpreted or could be considered intraspecific variation with respect to Anchiornis

facts.statement: The time range for Serikornis is recorded as 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)
